source_evidence: Borrowers of leveraged loans may go out of business or become unable to pay their debts. This risk could be heightened if interest rates rise or the economy declines.
answer: Default risk is the possibility that a borrower cannot repay a leveraged loan. Because these loans are made to borrowers with high debt levels and/or low credit ratings, lenders consider their default risk above average. A fund that holds leveraged loans could lose money if borrowers cannot pay. Even when a loan is secured by collateral, that collateral may not be worth enough to repay the lender. Default risk could be heightened if interest rates rise or the economy declines.
